key_insight: The paper argues that current world models are judged too much on frame prediction and too little on whether they maintain a persistent internal state over time. In short, they can look right moment-to-moment without truly remembering how the world continues when unobserved.
problem_solved: It addresses the evaluation blind spot in world-model benchmarks: most tests do not verify whether a model preserves object permanence, causal continuity, and hidden state across occlusion or missing observations.
method: Identifies the gap between visual realism and persistent world-state modeling in existing benchmarks.
Frames persistent state as a core requirement: the model should evolve an internal state independently of direct observation.
Evaluates or proposes benchmark criteria that test whether events and objects continue coherently when not explicitly visible.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shifts attention from generating plausible images to building and measuring models that truly understand dynamics over time. It can improve planning, robotics, simulation, and any system that must reason about unseen or delayed consequences.
visual_elements: Split-panel diagram showing 'rendering frames' vs 'persistent internal state'
Timeline of a hidden object/event continuing while occluded
Benchmark scorecard comparing visual fidelity and state persistence
Icon set for object permanence, memory, and causality
paper_title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
paper_authors: Jinpeng Lu, Dexu Zhu, Haoyuan Shi, Linghan Cai, Guo Tang
